item.title: Development :: [WIP] Tactical-RPG for the MS by cireza
item.description:
Author: cireza
Subject: [WIP] Tactical-RPG for the MS by cireza
Posted: Wed Nov 11, 2026 9:33 am (GMT 0)

Hello everyone,

I am sharing today the proof of concept I have been working on since this summer, after completing ReSeCom. Concerning ReSeCom, the game will release on Evercade in the Indie Collection 5 cartridge at the beginning of next year, and I am still looking into having a physical release on Master System, hopefully sometime next year.

The next game will be a Tactical-RPG. It is something I always wanted to make but felt like it was going to be too overwhelming. This is my third game already, close to 5 years have passed since I started doing this, so if I don't make it now I am not sure I will make it ever. This is why I decided to give a go. Thankfully I have earned a lot of experience with previous projets on how to organize my code and data structures.

The challenge of doing such a game on MS lies mainly around the VRAM and the palette. Shining Force games did make it to the GG, but they split the palette in 2, with colors reserved for the units, and others for the BG. It works, but it doesn't look great. Other games do manage to lock the 16 colors for everything : unit + map. This is what I am doing here. There was a lot of back and forth though on how to achieve the presentation.

Here you can see that the scale for the game is based on 3x3 tiles and units, which is pretty big (same size as Shining Force on MD). I have decided to use a clear palette to identify the walk area :


There will be traits for characters that tell us what they like and dislike. Window placement is dynamic to make sure that it doesn't come over the possible target areas (which are not implemented yet).


Night palette as well :




The engine manages up to 21 units (this uses around half of the VRAM for units alone) :


Finally here is a mock-up of how the battle scenes will look :

Here again choices have been made about the colors and palettes and how things are split. I wanted a symmetric system so in the end, you get the enemy + its BG on one palette and the ally + its BG on another. I have a set of locked in colors, and slot 0 is used for the blue/red color of the ally/enemy in the windows.

The game will be about optimizing your positive traits and exploiting the negative traits of the enemies to maximize damage.

You can also see on the screenshots that I managed to implement a height feature. Though I did take a shortcut here, because a proper perspective proved to difficult to implement, so I found a way to have a height system while still retaining a perfect 3x3 tile grid.

Here is the test map that I used to fine tune a lot of things :


Here are the things that are implemented :
- proper scrolling of the map + movement of cursor, with management of the edges of the map (this was new for me)
- units act by order depending on their speed
- walk area is calculated and takes into account enemy units, blocking tiles and slow tiles
- moving the unit to another location, then displays the windows
- goes on to the next unit automatically
- brand new police I have created, sadly Variable Width Font won't be in this game, I don't have enough VRAM for this
- dynamic calculation of the lifebars (tile forging)
- dynamic merging of the units in the background
- same for the battles, I have written a function to merge dynamically over the background the unit, I can select the size, shape and position

item.title: Made By AI :: The purpose of this forum, and rules
item.description:
Author: Maxim
Subject: The purpose of this forum, and rules
Posted: Wed Nov 11, 2026 6:26 am (GMT 0)

We are living in a time of technological change where people are able to use generative AI to produce many things far faster than in the past. We want to draw a distinction between creations for Sega 8-bit video games that were made using such tools, and those made by our community over the years using traditional techniques of doing all the work by hand.

This is a complex topic and a moving target. There is a clear difference between using AI to "vibe port" a game, or to generate some cover art, versus using it to help with some minor aspect of tooling or as a search/summarisation tool. For now, we are aiming to just label and segregate these topics so that it is made as clear as possible to the users that these are not completely "made by humans".

All topics titles must have "[AI]" at the start. All topics for AI-generated works must be in this forum.

If you think your topic has been moved here wrongly, because your use of AI was not significant enough to warrant calling it "made by AI", then please help us to clarify that usage and justify calling it "made by humans".

cireza wrote

Funny that you mention the color purple by the way, because when making the Sword of Stone, I ended up in a similar situation and the game did not have any purple at all. This frustrated me to no end.


Yeah, that one hurts

cireza wrote

A final thing I want to say in case some people don't realize this, is that targetting the same ROM size as on MegaDrive might prove challenging because you cannot use palette swaps for the various palettes of a single enemy : they are actually redrawn using different indexes of the palette. If I were you I wouldn't bother at all with trying to reach such a ROM a size for now and simply keep it below 1 MB.


I'm not too concerned about this. I want to see if I can get under 512 though. For flash carts with the 512KB limitation. I haven't explored optimization yet. I know there's opportunities, and compression options. I just haven't tested to see how it affects performance. I'm just glad the thing works 😆

item.title: Development :: RE: SMS Phantasy Star II
item.description:
Author: cireza
Posted: Tue Nov 10, 2026 12:17 pm (GMT 0)

xfixium wrote

Aye, excellent question. I think I may have done the palette design at least 4 times.


Thanks for sharing the complete set that you have generated, this clearly shows how much work you put into maximizing visibility. I think everything works well indeed, except maybe for a couple "orange" enemies on the dungeon BG. I suppose that you may plan different palettes for the BG ? Of course, they will not be strictly palette swaps. But this could help the few cases as you will know which enemy appears on which BG color. The dams also have color themes, this would work well.

Funny that you mention the color purple by the way, because when making the Sword of Stone, I ended up in a similar situation and the game did not have any purple at all. This frustrated me to no end.

A final thing I want to say in case some people don't realize this, is that targetting the same ROM size as on MegaDrive might prove challenging because you cannot use palette swaps for the various palettes of a single enemy : they are actually redrawn using different indexes of the palette. If I were you I wouldn't bother at all with trying to reach such a ROM a size for now and simply keep it below 1 MB.

item.title: Development :: RE: SMS Phantasy Star II
item.description:
Author: segarule
Posted: Tue Nov 10, 2026 9:01 am (GMT 0)

xfixium wrote
A demo is out, but not too much going on, it's basically a walking demo. You can visit a bunch of areas on Mota. Paseo, Oputa, Arima, Shure, Nido, and the Bio Systems lab. All the bridges are open, so you can explore most of Mota, except the areas that require the Jet Scooter. Random encounters happen. Pressing button 1 escapes the battle, button 2 cycles through 3 different test battle backgrounds. Pressing button 1 opens the menu when on the field. The only other menu available is the SYS menu. You can select the walking speed you desire from there. No data driven dialog text yet. The continue menu is just a mock up with no code behind it yet.

I had this close to a demo about roughly a year ago. But as luck would have it, my laptop died, and my motivation went out the window with it. But the last few weeks or so, I looked at the remaining items of my demo ready todo list, and got it done.

Some notes about it's current state. Most of the graphics conversion is done for the Mota towns. There are things I still want to adjust and redo however. The overworld will get a total re-vamp at some point. The battle backgrounds are placeholders. Except the VR one, which I consider done. The grass bg one is a PS1 bg, with some edits. The dungeon bg is a PSIV bg edited. So those will eventually be original graphics. Some of the enemies still need some TLC. I condensed the menus to save on RAM and screen real estate. Most main character sprites are done, or just need a little tweaking. Just missing Kain and Hugh. Probably some other notes I'm missing XD. I think that's it, for now.

Thanks for viewing.
